transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I've just been feeling really depressed and empty inside, and it's been going on for a very long time now. I've felt this constant sadness almost every day for over two years, and I just can't seem to shake it.
Have you experienced any periods of time during these two years where your mood was completely normal and you felt like yourself again, or has this low mood been present for most of every single day?

No, I haven't really had any periods where I felt completely normal or like my old self. It has been a continuous, heavy cloud over me almost every single day for the entire two years and three months. I just haven't been able to shake it at all.
During these past two years, have you struggled with other symptoms like changes in your appetite, difficulty sleeping, low energy, or feelings of low self-esteem?

Yes, my sleep has been terrible—I have a hard time falling asleep, wake up constantly, and always feel completely exhausted. My energy is just totally gone and I feel physically drained all the time. However, I haven't really noticed any major changes in my appetite or struggled with low self-esteem.

Have you experienced any episodes during these two years where your symptoms became significantly more intense, such as having thoughts that life is not worth living or losing interest in almost all of your usual activities?

No, I haven't experienced any severe drops like that, and I haven't had thoughts that life isn't worth living or lost interest in everything. Instead, my sadness, fatigue, and empty feelings have just remained at a constant, lingering level the entire time.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports a continuous low mood lasting over two years without any symptom-free intervals of more than two months, and specifically denies the severe, episodic, or vegetative symptoms (like significant appetite changes or total loss of interest) that would typically characterize a Major Depressive Disorder episode. Therefore, Persistent Depressive Disorder is now the primary and only candidate.
